aiInfra.headline: SK Hynix Tue close ₩1,443,000 (−10.09% vs Mon ₩1,605,000), KOSPI −5.46% to 6,035.35. Wed live 10:26 KST: SK ₩1,458,000 (+1.04%), Samsung ₩236,000 (+1.72%), KOSPI 6,079.69 (+0.73%); early bounce (KOSPI >6,100, SK ~₩1,478,000–1,497,000) faded.
aiInfra.why: Dead-cat-or-base test. Bounce is bargain buying with foreigners returning, not new fundamental news. Q3 earnings 27 Oct is the real check.

aiInfra.headline: CXMT follow-through: MU −3.62% to $953.19, AMAT −6.7% (worst in S&P), SKHY ADR −3.19%. Counterpoint: CXMT DRAM share 10% in Q2 2026 vs 4% a year earlier. CXMT has still given no 4F² spec, yield or volume; EUV-restricted.
aiInfra.why: Market is pricing a lower long-run DRAM margin ceiling. Thesis break needs yield/volume proof; until then this is multiple compression, not earnings damage.

aiInfra.headline: GOOGL: Gemini 4 Argon released to developers worldwide (intro $2/$10 per M tokens until 30 Nov, then $4/$20). Separately, GF Securities note says TPU v9 slipped ~3 weeks on EMIB substrate yield; sampling still Nov, volume shipments Q1 2028.
aiInfra.why: Model launch supports Cloud demand. TPU slip is a minor supply-chain timing item (broker note, unconfirmed by Google), not a capex cut.

aiInfra.headline: META +2.63% to $762.50, second day up on Muse Wonder; Rosenblatt says the model 'kills the bear case'.
aiInfra.why: Market now rewards META capex because it is producing a frontier model. Supports GPU/DC spend into 28 Oct earnings.

aiInfra.headline: SPCX −4.21% to $156.54 (vol 68M): worry over planned ~$40B debt ($10B loans + $30B IG bonds) for Nvidia GPUs, CDS wider; skepticism on ~$8B 800 MHz spectrum buy; agreed to testify Fri at NYC Council AI-safety probe; ARK sold ~$9.4M.
aiInfra.why: Leverage-funded AI capex is the same overhang hitting NBIS. Next unlock 24 Oct. Pivotal $230 / Stifel $190 PTs.

aiInfra.headline: NVDA +0.97% to $228.52, AMZN −0.37% to $258.58: no thesis-changing news (NVDA consumer DLSS 5 / RTX Spark; AWS routine launches incl. Claude Haiku 5.5 on Bedrock). Oracle +4.2%.
aiInfra.why: Hyperscaler/GPU side steady while memory and leveraged names absorb the selling.

macro.headline: Fed: Collins expects to raise rates 'a bit further before the end of the year'; Williams sees room for one more 2026 hike, no urgency, economy 'not overheating'. Markets price ~78% hold at 27–28 Oct, December hike more likely.

nbis.headline: Tue US cash $206.86 (−1.52% / −$3.20 vs $210.06); open $200.50, range $197.60–$207.92 (tested $200 support), vol ~17.5M ≈ avg; post $208.80 (+0.94%); cap ~$56.2B (271.86M sh); ≈ THB 6,938/sh at 33.54. −17.2% over 5 sessions from Tue 6 Oct $249.87.
nbis.why: Held $200 (Sept pivot lows) intraday; a decisive break below opens ~$195. Day move ordinary for NBIS beta; no FLAG.

nbis.headline: Only new EDGAR item: Form 4 filed 13 Oct (20:06 UTC) — CRO Marc Boroditsky sold 7,000 sh at $211.23 on 12 Oct (~$1.48M) under a 10b5-1 plan. No 6-K, no 13G/D since Goldman 13G/A 7 Oct.
nbis.why: Immaterial, pre-planned. No dilution, guidance or contract disclosure. Next earnings ~10 Nov.

nbis.headline: The Information (Sun): Anthropic has an unannounced multiyear cloud deal with IREN. No value, term, capacity or GPU config; neither company confirmed. Coverage cites it as a 'missed Anthropic' worry for NBIS.
nbis.why: Competition read, not lost business: NBIS never disclosed an Anthropic contract. Confirms frontier labs are diversifying across neoclouds, which is demand-positive but pressures pricing.

nbis.headline: Anthropic to give institutional investors its first Q3 financials today (Wed, SF HQ) ahead of a possible IPO reported for November.
nbis.why: Direct read on frontier-lab compute spend and ability to pay neocloud bills. Strong numbers support the NBIS demand case; any compute-cost restraint hurts it. Result lands ~Thu WITA.

nbis.headline: Funding-cost overhang widened: Goldman CEO Solomon warned AI-infra financing needs could pressure rates and 'the returns and the viability of certain projects'; IMF names an AI-investment pullback as the top global downside risk.
nbis.why: Same overhang as Hock Tan's 'capital is the constraint' (Mon). NBIS relies on converts/debt (Aug $5.75B converts); 10Y 5.22% keeps the cost of capital high.
nbis.source: The Core Quant (bank calls, IMF WEO)

soWhat: NBIS $206.86 held $200 (low $197.60), −17% in 5 sessions; only a CRO 10b5-1 Form 4 — still narrative, not news. Break of $195–200 is the line.
Anthropic Q3 to investors today + IREN deal report: frontier-lab demand real but spreading across neoclouds; watch for compute-spend detail.
